message:
fix(host): do not free a helper's memory unless it is confirmed dead

Product 2, test 2. Three real defects the reviewer found, plus the cap they asked to be enforced
rather than inferred.

The teardown called TerminateProcess, waited five seconds, IGNORED THE RESULT, and unmapped the
view regardless. A helper that outlives its kill is then writing into a released page. The kill
is now confirmed, and when it is not, nothing is released at all: the process handle, the
mapping and the view are held, and the next capture is refused with thumb_helper_lingering until
that process is finally seen to exit. One block held forever beats a page freed under a live
writer, and refusing bounds it at one rather than one per request.

That branch is unexercised, which is written on it. TerminateProcess does not fail for a process
this one started, so the confirmation always succeeds and removing the guard breaks no test. It
is a guard, not a tested behaviour, and the comment says so rather than letting a reader assume
coverage that is not there.

The concurrency cap is now a compare_exchange rather than an argument about the caller's shape.
Two dispatchers means two threads can ask at once; the second gets thumb_busy immediately. Two
simultaneous captures against a helper that never answers now cost 408ms at a 400ms deadline
instead of two deadlines, and removing the cap makes that check fail with "0 refused, 2 timed
out".

elapsedUs now includes the teardown. It was stamped before the destructor ran, so it described
the wait and not what the caller waited for -- the kill and its confirmation are on the caller's
clock too. The timed-out case reports 566ms against a 400ms deadline, and the ~166ms difference
is the kill confirmation that used to be invisible.

Two comments were wrong and are corrected where they live rather than only where they were used.
host_thumbnail_budget.hpp still claimed a single dispatcher and that the type needs no lock; that
was fixed at the call site and not at the definition, which is the copy a reader finds first. And
thumbnail_deadline_test.cpp explained WS_EX_NOREDIRECTIONBITMAP as the thing that forces the
request to the window -- that was the hypothesis, the measurement refuted it, and the comment
outlived the experiment. It made no difference: zero WM_PRINT either way.

The retry constants are pinned too -- three attempts, two seconds apart, sixty second cooldown,
one second deadline -- so changing one has to edit a test.

26 checks, three runs clean; the dispatcher suite and the rest unchanged and still green.
